verses.gurmukhi: ਬਿਆਹ ਸਮੈ ਜੈਸੇ ਦੁਹੂੰ ਓਰ ਗਾਈਅਤਿ ਗੀਤ ਏਕੈ ਹੁਇ ਲਭਤ ਏਕੈ ਹਾਨਿ ਕਾਨਿ ਜਾਨੀਐ ॥
verses.translit_en: biaaeh samai jaise dhuhoo(n) or gaieeat geet ekai hui labhat ekai haan kaan jaaneeaai ||

en.bdb: Just as in celebration of marriage, songs are sung both in the bride and bridegroom's house, the bridegroom's side stands to gain through dowry and arrival of the bride whereas the bride's family loses in wealth and their daughter.

verses.gurmukhi: ਦੁਹੂੰ ਦਲ ਬਿਖੈ ਜੈਸੇ ਬਾਜਤ ਨੀਸਾਨ ਤਾਨ ਕਾਹੂ ਕਉ ਜੈ ਕਾਹੂ ਕਉ ਪਰਾਜੈ ਪਹਿਚਾਨੀਐ ॥
verses.translit_en: dhuhoo(n) dhal bikhai jaise baajat neesaan taan kaahoo kau jai kaahoo kau paraajai pahichaaneeaai ||

en.bdb: Just as drums are beaten by both sides before commencement of battle, one wins and the other loses ultimately.

verses.gurmukhi: ਜੈਸੇ ਦੁਹੂੰ ਕੂਲਿ ਸਰਿਤਾ ਮੈ ਭਰਿ ਨਾਉ ਚਲੈ ਕੋਊ ਮਾਝਿ ਧਾਰਿ ਕੋਊ ਪਾਰਿ ਪਰਵਾਨੀਐ ॥
verses.translit_en: jaise dhuhoo(n) kool saritaa mai bhar naau chalai kouoo maajh dhaar kouoo paar paravaaneeaai ||

en.bdb: Just as a boat sets out fully loaded with passengers from both banks of a river, one sails across while the other may sink half way.

verses.gurmukhi: ਧਰਮ ਅਧਰਮ ਕਰਮ ਕੈ ਅਸਾਧ ਸਾਧ ਊਚ ਨੀਚ ਪਦਵੀ ਪ੍ਰਸਿਧ ਉਨਮਾਨੀਐ ॥੩੮੨॥
verses.translit_en: dharam adharam karam kai asaadh saadh uooch neech padhavee prasidh unamaaneeaai ||382||

en.bdb: Similarly, by virtue of their good deeds, the obedient Sikhs of the Guru achieve high status in society while those who indulge in vices are easily recognised by their bad deeds.  (382)
